## Headline read — the most replicable thing

Ben operates a multi-touch, region-specific outreach engine that leads with *proof of concept in their geography* (Riverina track record: 31 projects, 8,800 hectares, $500k+ in ACCU value) rather than generic features. He sequences emails across 3–4 touches with escalating stakes (intro → social proof → named case study → asset handoff), then moves fast to phone the moment there's any signal, using calls to compress discovery into a single conversation and lock in next-step meetings.

## Conversation openers

### cold outbound (Wagyu/beef breeders, industry-sourced list)

**Pattern.** Opens with personal credential + specific peer outcome + permission-based soft call-to-action. Leads with 'I found your contact via the Wagyu Association' to establish legitimacy, immediately names a comparable producer (Adam and Tracy Gunthorpe: 18,000 credits, no herd quality compromise), links to case study, then offers two low-friction entry points (call or calendar).

**Verbatim:**
> "Hi Richard, Ben from AgriProve here. I found your contact via the Wagyu Association and wanted to share how top breeders are earning carbon credits—without compromising herd quality or brand. For example, producers like Adam and Tracy Gunthorpe boosted carrying capacity and earned 18,000 credits in a few years through improved management."
> "Would a quick call this week suit? Or ring me any time on +61 485 853 826."

### cold outbound (regional/geography-targeted, grain/mixed farming)

**Pattern.** Opens with place-based insight (soil type + carbon sink mechanics + rainfall = opportunity). Leads with local credibility ('proud Albury-based business'), then immediately lands with region-specific track record (31 projects, 8,800 ha, $500k+, 'more ACCUs than any other soil carbon developer'), frames it as 'operational not experimental', then conditional qualification gate (>400 ha).

**Verbatim:**
> "G'Day Jonathan, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as a proud Albury-based business in the region, I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the Riverina region. Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural 'carbon sink' where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years."
> "Our Riverina Track Record: 31 registered AgriProve soil carbon projects across the region equating to 8,800 total hectares. 13,055 ACCUs issued to Riverina farmers to date worth over half a million dollars. We've issued more ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) in the Riverina than any other soil carbon developer. This isn't experimental, it's operational."

### re-engagement (contact in database, known prospect, new financial year trigger)

**Pattern.** Acknowledges prior relationship ('we had a note to reach out'), frames timing as new-year opportunity, sets a low time commitment (20-minute chat), offers direct phone contact as alternative to booking link.

**Verbatim:**
> "Hi Daniel, I hope this finds you well. We haven't met before, my name is Ben and I was going through our database and we had a note to reach out to you in the new financial year regarding the potential of a soil carbon project with AgriProve. Would you be open to a 20-minute chat to explore how it could work on your property? Or feel free to give me a buzz directly on +61 485 853 826."

## Discovery questions

- **Qualification via land tenure + existing carbon/management program overlap. Asks whether prospect already enrolled in Ecological Benefits Scheme, has existing land management practices, or has prior RCS/Maia involvement. Designed to surface disqualifiers early and identify upsell vs. net-new scenarios.** — _surfaces:_ Identifies whether prospect is truly greenfield or already locked into competing scheme; allows Ben to either disqualify quickly or position AgriProve as complementary.
  > "Already has land under the Ecological benefits scheme, avoided clearing projects. Has been managing stocking rates and pasture seeding for the last 10 years, may not be much benefit to start a carbon project; gains may have already been realised."
  > "(Internal note post-call) 'Not a Landholder = Not a lead' / 'Not interested = Disqualified'"
- **ACCU value interest-check + co-product compatibility. Asks directly about ACCU value expectations and whether prospect runs other managed enterprises (tree plantings, livestock quality standards) that could conflict.** — _surfaces:_ Tests whether prospect is commodity-focused (ACCUs only) or ecosystem-thinking; reveals secondary business priorities that might affect project design.
  > "What is their value? Do you do any tree plantings in this space?"

## Transitions

### From email engagement (open/reply received) → phone call

Moves to phone call *within 24-48 hours* of any email reply. Does not loop email. Confirms receipt verbally, restates value thesis briefly, books specific next meeting with agenda and participants named.

> "Thanks Amanda, I hope you had a good weekend. I'll give a call later today."
> "(Post-call note) 'Outbound from Ben — brief 1m02s check-in following an earlier exchange (hard-copy paperwork has now arrived). Amanda just back from a trip up north, first work back, hopes to get into the office tomorrow to look at things. Confirmed hard-copy materials received; Amanda has Ben on her list to address. Action: Ben to touch base again later this week / next.'"

### From initial discovery call → farm visit / project planning meeting

Books a named, high-stakes follow-up meeting with specific agenda, third-party present (Head of Operations or AgriProve team lead), and commercial terms explicitly on the table. Frames meeting as 'clarify final key concerns and specific questions regarding Key Commercial Terms with the intention finalizing the document and moving forward.'

> "The aim of this meeting with Will is to clarify the final key concerns and specific questions regarding your Key Commercial Terms with the intention finalizing the document and moving forward to registering a soil carbon project with AgriProve."

### From discovery call (secondary questions raised, e.g., tree planting, land management partner) → partner coordination + parallel track

Immediately escalates to partner (Verterra for land management) while keeping soil carbon project momentum alive. Explicitly states: 'I'll touch base with our partners [Verterra] today for you. It would still be worth setting up a call to cover the soil carbon project while I engage with [partner]... as there are a few layers to get through before we even handover to the AgriProve operations team.'

> "Thanks Dean, I'll touch base with our partners Verterra today for you. It would still be worth setting up a call to cover the soil carbon project while I engage with Verterra so we can get the ball rolling as there are a few layers to get through before we even handover to the AgriProve operations team."

## Customer archetypes — who they engaged well

### Premium livestock operator (Wagyu/beef breeder) – mid-to-large holding, export-quality focused, seeking new revenue without compromising herd genetics or brand positioning

**Characteristics.** Contacted via industry association (Wagyu Association); concerns about herd quality + export standards; interested in ACCU value + scalability; often multi-generation family operation; time-poor (travel, farm demands)

**Approach.** Opens with peer proof (Gunthorpe: 18,000 ACCUs without quality loss), frames carbon as 'supporting premium production and export standards,' offers free ACCU potential estimate via platform signup, emphasizes non-invasive integration. Sequences 4 emails over 7–10 days, then moves to phone for deeper discovery. Schedules farm visit with operations personnel present to signal credibility.

**Example.** Amanda Mahy (Colorado Cattle Co) – Sept 1–Feb 6 nurture cycle; Richard Cox (Wagyu Association list) – Sept 1 through April multi-month engagement with seasonal call-backs.

### Regional grain/mixed farmer – 400+ ha, established land management practices, Riverina/Albury geography, potentially already in Ecological Benefits Scheme or RCS

**Characteristics.** Receptive to place-based messaging; responsive to peer proof in their region; time-poor during season; may have prior carbon/environmental program overlap (disqualifier if gains already realized); interested in operational clarity before commitment

**Approach.** Leads with region-specific soil science + track record (31 projects, 8,800 ha, $500k+ Riverina-specific). Offers regional case study (Ben Cassidy, Ariah Park, 1,000 ha, 8.03 ACCUs/ha/yr). Qualifies hard on prior program overlap; if clear, moves to phone for 20-min discovery and farm visit booking. Names commercial terms explicitly in meeting invite.

**Example.** Jonathan Harpley (Growth Farms, Riverina) – Dec 5–April 20 engagement; Dean Jonsson (Wombinoo Station, Qld) – March 2 through May 13 multi-touch with partner (Verterra) parallel track.

### Database re-engagement prospect – known to AgriProve via prior outreach or referral, now triggered by new FY or seasonal window

**Characteristics.** Lower cold resistance; prior relationship context available; often respond same-day to 'new FY' framing; may have scheduling delays but receptive when contacted; benefit from explicit time-window commitment ('touch base later this week/next')

**Approach.** Acknowledges prior database note ('we had a note to reach out'), frames new FY as clean entry point, offers low-commitment discovery (20-min chat), provides direct phone alternative to booking link. Tolerates reasonable delays; does not escalate pressure.

**Example.** Daniel Gazzola (July 14, 2025 FY re-engagement) – same-day reply, Ben called same-day.

### Strategic partnership prospect – secondary land management need (tree planting, pastoral improvement via Verterra or equivalent partner)

**Characteristics.** Larger holdings, complex management goals, may be stalled on single-product decision but responsive to bundled offering; benefit from explicit partner coordination messaging

**Approach.** Identifies partner need in discovery, immediately coordinates with partner (e.g., 'I'll touch base with our partners Verterra today for you') while keeping AgriProve soil carbon momentum parallel. Books separate agenda items; signals 'layers to get through' candidly to set expectation. Does not try to own the full opportunity alone.

**Example.** Dean Jonsson (Wombinoo Station) – tree planting interest + soil carbon = Verterra + AgriProve parallel tracks, May 11–May 13.

## Anti-patterns visible

- **Email looping after objection or soft rejection. Once a prospect has expressed disqualifier or lack of interest, Ben tends to continue sequencing emails rather than moving to phone or re-qualifying.** — Daniel Gazzola: Strong same-day response ('yes, I'm available tomorrow for a chat, 0427 691 891') but no call transcript visible in corpus, suggesting either call was not logged or did not proceed as planned. Single re-engagement cycle without visible follow-up completion.
- **Inconsistent call logging / transcript capture. Multiple call entries show only 'Outbound answered call via Ben Payne' with no notes or outcome recorded. Makes it impossible to assess discovery depth, objection handling, or meeting-lock success on individual calls.** — Dan Burnham: 3 calls Feb 24, March 10 (2026) marked as 'Outbound answered call via Ben Payne' with Recording IDs but zero notes on conversation outcome. Dean Jonsson: 5 calls over March 2–May 13 with only 1 note (May 13 voicemail transcript). Jonathan Harpley: 4 calls April 15–April 20 (2 inbound, 2 outbound) with no call notes. This is a systemic logging gap, not necessarily a rep behaviour failure, but it obscures quality of discovery and objection handling.
